A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GeoRA and contain readable, matchable methods, experiments, equations, tables and figures. All pages were inspected. v1 ends with references and has no appendices; v3 includes readable Appendices A–D.

before.justification: v1 reports original RLVR training outcomes, benchmark evaluations, efficiency measurements, ablations and geometric analyses in Tables 1–4 and Figures 3–6.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds medical and coding evaluations, mask-overlap measurements, initialization profiling and extended model evaluations, including results in Appendices B–D.

M1.justification: Section 3, Equations (1)–(8), retains the same mask union, top-r SVD initialization, frozen scaled residual and forward computation. The added pseudocode and randomized-SVD discussion document the method and implementation options without establishing a changed core procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds medical RLVR using AlphaMed19K with MedQA, MedMCQA and PubMedQA evaluation, and coding RLVR using Eurus-2-RL-Data with LiveCodeBench, HumanEval and MBPP evaluation. It also adds IFEval and TruthfulQA to OOD coverage. DeepMath-103K, GSM8K and HumanEval were already used in v1.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds the original pre-RLVR Base model as a comparator for both backbones. FullFT, SparseFT, LoRA, PiSSA and MiLoRA remain in the matched mathematical comparison. The new medical and coding comparisons use Base, FullFT and LoRA.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce Qwen2.5-1.5B and Qwen3-32B configurations, medical test-split validation and option-matching rewards, and coding verification through executable test cases with a 2048-token response budget. Initialization profiling spans 8B–72B models. The retained mathematical setup still specifies GRPO, rank 16 and rho 0.2; newly disclosed settings do not establish changes to those existing experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds mask-overlap analysis (Table 5), analysis of actual FullFT update spectra (Figure 6b), and initialization-cost profiling (Table 7). Appendix D supplies explicit rank and sparsity sweep curves for robustness that v1 only summarized. Existing initialization/mask ablations and learning-rate/KL stress tests are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix C.1 newly specifies a single random run; v1 gives no run count. No repeated-run uncertainty estimates or significance tests are added. This is newly disclosed run information, not evidence that the number of runs decreased.

E6.justification: Table 1 extensions and new Tables 2, 5, 7 and 8 add substantial results; for example, GeoRA's medical and coding averages are 73.69 and 79.65. Retained main per-task, efficiency, ablation and alignment table values are unchanged. Figure 3 also revises plotted step-500 accuracy: LoRA approximately 19.89 to 19.39 and GeoRA 22.29 to 22.69, while retaining their final values.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds a Frobenius-optimality proposition for truncated Geo-SVD, adapter-gradient formulas in Equation (12), and computational complexity analysis. Its function-preservation proposition largely restates the initialization identity already explained in v1. These are limited mathematical additions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion expand the claimed empirical scope from mathematical RLVR to mathematics, medicine and coding across 1.5B–32B models. v1's mathematical SOTA assertion is removed. The central geometry-aware initialization and stable, efficient adaptation contributions remain.

C2.justification: v3 substantially qualifies explanations that previously treated tail components as noise, KL spikes as establishing collapse's root cause, and GeoRA as strictly trust-region safe. It adds mask-complementarity and measured initialization-overhead interpretations. The OOD discussion also replaces v1's incorrect best-GPQA claim with strongest-or-near-strongest wording. The Limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C add pseudocode, SVD profiling, alpha 32, all-linear adapter targets, AdamW/bfloat16, batch size 128, eight rollouts, KL coefficient 0.001, GPU configurations and task-specific verification rules. These substantially expand reproducibility information. However, Algorithm 1 uses an unscaled residual subtraction, conflicting with the alpha/r scaling retained in Equation (4).

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds continual-learning and multi-task PEFT references, and the expanded experiments introduce benchmark and domain citations. The main positioning around RLVR geometry and spectral PEFT remains. Author, year and publication changes for existing references do not represent new cited works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, experimental discussion, mechanism narrative and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. Experiments are reorganized into setup, main results, stability/efficiency and ablation subsections, and Appendices A–D are introduced. The method exposition remains largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 adds Base rows and two OOD columns while removing the ID-average column; four new tables are introduced. Figure 3 changes from grouped bars to lines, Figure 6 expands to two panels, and Figure 7 and Algorithm 1 are added. Several retained displays are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the paper's assessability and supporting evidence: Base comparisons clarify forgetting, actual FullFT update spectra better support the low-rank motivation, and Appendix C fills major reproducibility gaps. Medical/coding evaluations and initialization profiling directly test broader applicability and practical efficiency, while interpretations become better qualified. Single-run evidence still limits confidence, and Algorithm 1 introduces a scaling inconsistency, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains.
